context: The data is a frozen OpenFlights snapshot (routes from June 2014, commit e539814f664c): 6,071 IATA-coded airports and 37,041 one-way flights, each a directed pair of airports with the airline dropped. A route may change planes at any airport, and any valid sequence of real one-way flights from an origin airport to a destination airport is accepted; it need not be the shortest. Place lookup: exactly three capital letters (spaces around them trimmed) is an IATA code; anything else is a city name, matched case- and accent-insensitively, and 'City, Country' restricts to that country when the whole text is not itself a city name. London names LCY, LGW, LHR, LOZ, LTN, STN and YXU. The data contains the one-way flights HOU to ATL and ATL to LHR. Statuses are decided in this order: no_such_airport when the origin (then the destination) is an unknown IATA code; no_such_city when the origin (then the destination) is unknown city text; same_place when an airport is in both the origin and destination sets; no_flight when no origin airport has any flight out or no destination airport has any flight in; no_route when there are flights but no connection of any length; otherwise found. Non-found outputs must have an empty airports list; a found output must list IATA codes with no repeats, starting at an origin airport and ending at a destination airport.
